scope.reason: Native AOT rules hold for all hand-written F#, so code can move between tests, tools and the binary.
No I/O outside Eff is a rule for production code, built-in extensions included; tests and tools are imperative shells. The samples prove the rules.

allow.reason: Process entry point: writes the outcome of the pure Cli.run to stdout and stderr.
Entry point of an F# extension process: serves the extension protocol on standard input and output, and sends what extensions write to Console.Out to standard error.
IClock interpreter: the only reader of the system clock and the only real delay.
IIds interpreter: the only reader of the OS random number generator.
IFs/IFsRead interpreter: the only code that touches the local filesystem.
IShell interpreter: the only code that starts and controls processes.
ITerminal interpreter: the only code that starts and controls processes on pseudo-terminals (posix_spawn with a PTY, CreateProcessW with ConPTY).
The P/Invoke layer of the ITerminal interpreter: `ioctl` picks the declaration for the platform's variadic calling convention.
The SQLite binding itself: its P/Invoke layer (EFF008) and its own API (EFF009).
--build-info reports the version of the SQLite linked into the binary; it touches no database.
EventLog and SnapshotStore interpreter: the event database (one writer thread, pooled readers).
IBlobs interpreter: the only code that reads and writes blob files (temporary files, atomic renames, syncs) and their SQLite index.
IFetch interpreter: the installer's only HTTP client; it streams each download into the file it is given (FileStream).
IInstallFiles interpreter: the installer's only code that touches the disk directly (unpacking, hashing, deleting trees, atomic replacement, lock files).
FsOps interpreter: ranged reads (seek) and atomic writes (a temporary file renamed over the target, keeping its Unix mode).
FsOps.Watch interpreter: the only FileSystemWatcher; its events go into a ChangeQueue that the clock debounces.
Spill interpreter: appends overflowing process output to files in envd's state directory and reads them back for resumed attachments.
envd's platform detection at startup: PATH (which shell), the locale variables (terminal defaults) and the workspace's case sensitivity, read once as values.
envd's composition root: the workspace (current directory), the per-user state directory (HOME or LOCALAPPDATA) and its layout.
Dials local listeners (loopback, Unix socket, named pipe) for WebSocket clients: the only outgoing connection code.
The number-formatting scenario checks that composite String.Format behaves identically on the JIT and under Native AOT.
The diff harness canary must differ between JIT and native: Assembly.Location is empty only in a native binary.
Sample proving that an allow entry suppresses exactly the codes it lists.
